name.zh: 弗罗茨瓦夫（拉丁名弗拉蒂斯拉维亚）

polity.en: Piast Poland, then the Silesian Piast duchies
polity.zh: 皮雅斯特波兰，后为西里西亚皮雅斯特诸公国

name.zh: 布雷斯劳（捷克语弗拉蒂斯拉夫）

polity.zh: 哈布斯堡君主国（波希米亚王冠领地）

summary.en: The chief city of Silesia became a bishopric in 1000 under the Piasts, passed to the Bohemian crown in 1335, to the Habsburgs and in 1742 to Prussia. As German Breslau it was declared a fortress in 1945 and largely destroyed; after the war it became Polish Wrocław, its German population expelled and replaced by Poles, many from Lwów.
summary.zh: 西里西亚的首府于1000年在皮雅斯特王朝治下设立主教区，1335年归属波希米亚王冠，后归哈布斯堡家族，1742年归普鲁士。作为德国城市布雷斯劳，它在1945年被宣布为要塞，几乎被摧毁；战后成为波兰的弗罗茨瓦夫，德国居民被驱逐，取而代之的是波兰人，其中许多来自利沃夫。

sources.title: Norman Davies & Roger Moorhouse, Microcosm: Portrait of a Central European City (2002)

name.zh: 利沃夫（拉丁名莱奥波利斯）

polity.zh: 波兰王国、波兰—立陶宛联邦
哈布斯堡君主国（加利西亚首府）
纳粹德国占领（加利西亚区）
苏联（乌克兰苏维埃社会主义共和国）

summary.en: Founded in the mid-13th century by King Daniel of Galicia and named after his son Lev, the city was taken by Casimir III of Poland in 1349, became Austrian Lemberg in 1772 and Polish Lwów in 1918. The Holocaust destroyed its large Jewish community, and after 1944 its Poles were moved west; it is now a centre of Ukrainian culture.
summary.zh: 该城由加利西亚国王达尼洛于13世纪中叶建立，以其子列夫命名，1349年被波兰国王卡齐米日三世攻取，1772年成为奥地利的伦贝格，1918年成为波兰的利沃夫。大屠杀摧毁了城中庞大的犹太社区，1944年后波兰居民被迁往西部；今天它是乌克兰文化的中心。

sources.title: Christopher Hann & Paul Robert Magocsi (eds.), Galicia: A Multicultured Land (2005)
UNESCO World Heritage: L'viv – the Ensemble of the Historic Centre

note: The founding date (first mention 1256) is approximate; Lviv became the Galician capital around 1272. The brief West Ukrainian People's Republic of November 1918 is folded into the 1918 entry.

polity.en: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth (capital of the Grand Duchy)
polity.zh: 波兰—立陶宛联邦（立陶宛大公国首府）

polity.en: German occupation, then contested by Lithuania, Soviet Russia and Poland
polity.zh: 德国占领，后为立陶宛、苏俄和波兰争夺
苏联（立陶宛苏维埃社会主义共和国），1941—1944年被德国占领

summary.en: First mentioned in Grand Duke Gediminas's letters of 1323, Vilnius was the capital of Lithuania, a Polish-speaking city of the Commonwealth, the Russian provincial town of Vilna and, as "the Jerusalem of Lithuania", a great centre of Jewish learning. Seized by Poland in 1920, it was returned to Lithuania in 1939 and became its capital again in 1990.
summary.zh: 维尔纽斯最早见于1323年格迪米纳斯大公的书信，曾是立陶宛首都、联邦时代以波兰语为主的城市、俄国的省城维尔纳，又被誉为“立陶宛的耶路撒冷”，是犹太学术的重镇。1920年被波兰夺取，1939年归还立陶宛，1990年再度成为立陶宛首都。

sources.title: Theodore R. Weeks, Vilnius between Nations, 1795–2000 (2015)
UNESCO World Heritage: Vilnius Historic Centre

polity.en: Contested between Great Moravia, Bavaria and the Magyars
polity.zh: 大摩拉维亚、巴伐利亚与马扎尔人争夺之地

polity.en: Habsburg Kingdom of Hungary (capital and coronation city)
polity.zh: 哈布斯堡治下的匈牙利王国（首都、加冕之城）

name.zh: 普雷斯堡 / 波若尼 / 普雷绍波克

polity.zh: 匈牙利王国（哈布斯堡君主国）

summary.en: Recorded as Brezalauspurc at the battle of 907, the Danube town was Hungarian Pozsony and German Pressburg for nine centuries, serving as Hungary's capital and coronation city after the Ottomans took Buda. In 1919 it joined Czechoslovakia under the new name Bratislava, and it has been the capital of independent Slovakia since 1993.
summary.zh: 这座多瑙河畔城市在907年的战役记载中被称作布雷扎拉乌斯普尔茨，此后九个世纪是匈牙利的波若尼、德意志人的普雷斯堡；奥斯曼人攻占布达后，它成为匈牙利的首都和加冕之城。1919年它以新名布拉迪斯拉发并入捷克斯洛伐克，1993年起为独立的斯洛伐克首都。

sources.title: Pál Engel, The Realm of St Stephen (2001)

note: The identification of Brezalauspurc with Bratislava is generally but not universally accepted.

name.zh: 腓力波利斯（普尔普德瓦）

polity.zh: 奥德里西亚色雷斯王国（罗马附庸）

name.zh: 腓力波利斯（特里蒙提乌姆）
腓力波利斯 / 普罗夫迪夫

polity.en: Byzantine Empire, with periods of Bulgarian rule
polity.zh: 拜占庭帝国，间有保加利亚统治时期
东鲁米利亚（奥斯曼自治省）

summary.en: One of Europe's oldest continuously inhabited cities, the Thracian Pulpudeva was refounded by Philip II of Macedon as Philippopolis and became the Roman capital of Thrace. Contested between Byzantium and Bulgaria, it was Ottoman Filibe from the 1360s, capital of autonomous Eastern Rumelia in 1878–1885, and then united with Bulgaria.
summary.zh: 普罗夫迪夫是欧洲持续有人居住的最古老城市之一。色雷斯人的普尔普德瓦被马其顿的腓力二世重建为腓力波利斯，后成为罗马色雷斯行省的首府。它在拜占庭与保加利亚之间几度易手，1360年代起为奥斯曼的菲利贝，1878—1885年为自治省东鲁米利亚首府，随后并入保加利亚。

sources.title: R. J. Crampton, A Concise History of Bulgaria (2005)

note: The Ottoman conquest is dated 1363 or 1364; medieval rule alternated between Byzantium and Bulgaria and is summarised in one entry.

polity.en: Thracian Serdi, Roman Empire from the 1st century
polity.zh: 色雷斯塞尔迪人，1世纪起属罗马帝国

name.zh: 塞尔迪卡 / 特里亚迪察
特里亚迪察 / 斯雷德茨

summary.en: Roman Serdica, where Galerius issued his edict of toleration in 311, was taken by Khan Krum in 809 and known to the Bulgarians as Sredets. The name Sofia, from its church of Holy Wisdom, came into use in the 14th century. Ottoman from 1382, it was chosen as capital of the new Bulgarian state in 1879.
summary.zh: 罗马时代的塞尔迪卡是伽列里乌斯于311年颁布宽容敕令之地，809年被克鲁姆可汗攻取，保加利亚人称之为斯雷德茨。“索非亚”之名源自城中的圣智慧教堂，14世纪开始使用。1382年起归奥斯曼统治，1879年被选为新生保加利亚国家的首都。

sources.title: R. J. Crampton, A Concise History of Bulgaria (2005)

note: Dates of Bulgarian recovery in the 1190s are approximate.

polity.zh: 利沃尼亚骑士团（利沃尼亚联盟），汉萨同盟城市
瑞典帝国（爱沙尼亚公国）
苏联（爱沙尼亚苏维埃社会主义共和国），1941—1944年被德国占领

summary.en: King Valdemar II of Denmark took the Estonian stronghold of Lindanise in 1219, and as German-speaking Reval the town flourished in the Hanseatic League under Danish, Livonian Order and Swedish rule. Russian from 1710, it became the capital of independent Estonia under its Estonian name, Tallinn ("Danish town"), in 1918.
summary.zh: 1219年丹麦国王瓦尔德马二世攻占爱沙尼亚人的林达尼塞要塞。在丹麦、利沃尼亚骑士团和瑞典统治下，讲德语的雷瓦尔作为汉萨同盟城市繁荣兴盛。1710年起归俄国，1918年以爱沙尼亚语名称塔林（意为“丹麦人的城”）成为独立的爱沙尼亚首都。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Centre (Old Town) of Tallinn
Toivo U. Raun, Estonia and the Estonians (2nd ed. 2001)

polity.zh: 多尔帕特采邑主教区（利沃尼亚联盟）
俄罗斯沙皇国（利沃尼亚战争期间）

name.zh: 多尔帕特 / 杰尔普特

polity.zh: 俄罗斯帝国（俄罗斯化时期）
苏联（爱沙尼亚苏维埃社会主义共和国）

summary.en: Yaroslav the Wise founded a fort called Yuryev here in 1030 on the site of the Estonian Tarbatu. As German Dorpat it was the seat of a Livonian prince-bishop and, from 1632, of a Swedish university. Russia renamed it Yuryev in 1893; the Treaty of Tartu (1920) recognised Estonian independence.
summary.zh: 1030年，智者雅罗斯拉夫在爱沙尼亚人的塔尔巴图旧址上建起名为尤里耶夫的要塞。作为德语城市多尔帕特，它曾是利沃尼亚采邑主教的驻地，1632年起又有瑞典人创办的大学。1893年俄国将其改名为尤里耶夫；1920年的《塔尔图和约》承认了爱沙尼亚的独立。

sources.title: Toivo U. Raun, Estonia and the Estonians (2001)

note: The 1030 foundation and the Estonian recapture in 1061 come from the Rus' chronicles.

polity.zh: 弗拉基米尔—苏兹达尔；下诺夫哥罗德—苏兹达尔公国

polity.en: Grand Principality of Moscow; Tsardom of Russia
polity.zh: 莫斯科大公国、俄罗斯沙皇国
俄罗斯帝国、苏维埃俄国

summary.en: Founded by Grand Prince Yuri II of Vladimir in 1221 at the confluence of the Oka and Volga, the city raised the Minin–Pozharsky militia in 1612 and hosted Russia's greatest trade fair. Renamed Gorky after its native writer Maxim Gorky in 1932, it was closed to foreigners; Andrei Sakharov was exiled there in 1980–1986.
summary.zh: 该城于1221年由弗拉基米尔大公尤里二世建于奥卡河与伏尔加河交汇处，1612年在此组建了米宁和波扎尔斯基的民军，后来又举办俄国最大的集市。1932年以本地出身的作家马克西姆·高尔基之名改称高尔基，对外国人封闭；1980—1986年安德烈·萨哈罗夫被流放于此。

polity.zh: 苏维埃俄国（1918—1919年为白军控制）

summary.en: Founded in 1723 by Vasily Tatishchev and Georg Wilhelm de Hennin as an ironworks town in the Urals, the city was named after Catherine I. The last tsar and his family were shot here in July 1918; renamed Sverdlovsk after the Bolshevik Yakov Sverdlov in 1924, it regained its old name in 1991.
summary.zh: 1723年，瓦西里·塔季谢夫和格奥尔格·威廉·德亨宁在乌拉尔山区建立这座冶铁城，以叶卡捷琳娜一世命名。1918年7月末代沙皇一家在此被枪决；1924年以布尔什维克雅科夫·斯维尔德洛夫之名改称斯维尔德洛夫斯克，1991年恢复旧名。

sources.title: Mark Steinberg & Vladimir Khrustalëv, The Fall of the Romanovs (1995)

note: Located geographically in Asia (east of the Urals) but administratively and historically part of European Russia's Urals region.

polity.zh: 俄罗斯帝国，内战中多方争夺

苏联（乌克兰苏维埃社会主义共和国）

polity.en: Ukraine; under Russian control since 2014 (annexation claimed in 2022, not internationally recognised)
polity.zh: 乌克兰；2014年起处于俄罗斯控制之下（2022年俄方宣布吞并，未获国际承认）

summary.en: The Welsh industrialist John Hughes founded a steelworks in the Donbas steppe in 1869, and the settlement grew as Yuzovka. Renamed after Stalin in 1924 and Donetsk during de-Stalinisation in 1961, the coal and steel city has been held by Russian-backed forces since 2014 and claimed as annexed by Russia in 2022, a claim rejected by Ukraine and the UN General Assembly.
summary.zh: 1869年，威尔士实业家约翰·休斯在顿巴斯草原建起炼钢厂，聚落发展为尤佐夫卡。1924年以斯大林之名改称，1961年去斯大林化时改称顿涅茨克。这座煤炭钢铁城市自2014年起被俄罗斯支持的武装控制，2022年俄罗斯宣布将其吞并，乌克兰和联合国大会均不予承认。

sources.title: Theodore H. Friedgut, Iuzovka and Revolution, 2 vols. (1989–1994)
UN General Assembly resolution ES-11/4 (12 October 2022)

note: Renamed Stalin in 1924 and Stalino in 1929–1931 (sources vary); both forms are given in one entry.

polity.zh: 俄罗斯帝国，内战中多方争夺

polity.zh: 苏联（乌克兰苏维埃社会主义共和国）

name.zh: 第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克

summary.en: Founded after the Russian conquest of the steppe and named "Glory of Catherine", the city was briefly renamed Novorossiysk by Paul I. In 1926 it became Dnipropetrovsk, after the river and the Bolshevik Hryhorii Petrovsky, a centre of Soviet rocket and steel industry; Ukraine's decommunisation law led to the shorter name Dnipro in 2016.
summary.zh: 该城在俄国征服草原后建立，名为“叶卡捷琳娜的荣耀”，曾一度被保罗一世改称新罗西斯克。1926年以第聂伯河和布尔什维克彼得罗夫斯基之名改称第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克，成为苏联火箭和钢铁工业中心；2016年乌克兰“去共产主义化”法令使其改名为更短的第聂伯。

note: The first Yekaterinoslav (1776) stood near the Kilchen river and was moved to the present site in 1787.

polity.zh: 民族大迁徙时期诸部族，约1000年起属匈牙利王国

polity.zh: 哈布斯堡君主国；1867年起属匈牙利王国（奥匈帝国）
匈牙利（第二次维也纳仲裁）

summary.en: Roman Napoca became a municipium under Hadrian. Medieval Kolozsvár, with its Saxon burghers, was the birthplace of King Matthias Corvinus and a chief city of Transylvania. It passed to Romania in 1920, back to Hungary in 1940–1944, and in 1974 the Ceaușescu regime added the Roman name to stress the city's Latin past.
summary.zh: 罗马时代的纳波卡在哈德良时期获得自治市地位。中世纪的科洛日堡有撒克逊市民，是国王马加什·科尔温的出生地和特兰西瓦尼亚的主要城市之一。1920年归罗马尼亚，1940—1944年重归匈牙利；1974年齐奥塞斯库政权为强调该城的拉丁渊源，在城名后加上了罗马时代的名字。

sources.title: Holly Case, Between States: The Transylvanian Question and the European Idea during World War II (2009)

note: Dates for the post-Roman period are approximate; Clus is first recorded in 1213.

polity.zh: 塞尔维亚国家、泽塔公国

polity.en: Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; Serbia and Montenegro
polity.zh: 南斯拉夫联盟共和国、塞尔维亚和黑山

summary.en: Near the ruins of Roman Doclea, the medieval market town of Podgorica ("under the little hill") was first recorded in 1326 and fell to the Ottomans in 1474. Montenegro gained it in 1878. Rebuilt after heavy bombing in the Second World War, it was renamed Titograd in 1946 and became the capital of Montenegro, independent since 2006.
summary.zh: 波德戈里察（意为“小山之下”）靠近罗马城市多克莱亚的遗址，这座中世纪集镇最早见于1326年的记载，1474年落入奥斯曼人之手，1878年归黑山。二战中遭猛烈轰炸后重建，1946年改名铁托格勒并成为黑山首府；黑山自2006年起独立。

sources.title: Elizabeth Roberts, Realm of the Black Mountain: A History of Montenegro (2007)

polity.zh: 卡林西亚公国（施庞海姆家族），后属波希米亚

polity.zh: 奥地利帝国、奥匈帝国（卡尼奥拉首府）

polity.en: Yugoslavia (capital of Slovenia); Italian and German occupation 1941–1945
polity.zh: 南斯拉夫（斯洛文尼亚首府）；1941—1945年被意大利、德国占领

summary.en: Roman Emona was destroyed by the Huns in 452. The medieval town of Laibach, first recorded in 1144, was the Habsburg capital of Carniola for six centuries and briefly the capital of Napoleon's Illyrian Provinces. Rebuilt after the 1895 earthquake and shaped by the architect Jože Plečnik, Ljubljana became the capital of independent Slovenia in 1991.
summary.zh: 罗马城市埃莫纳于452年被匈人摧毁。中世纪城镇莱巴赫最早见于1144年的记载，六个世纪间是哈布斯堡治下卡尼奥拉的首府，曾短暂作为拿破仑伊利里亚行省的首府。1895年地震后重建，并经建筑师约热·普列赤涅克塑造，卢布尔雅那于1991年成为独立的斯洛文尼亚首都。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: The works of Jože Plečnik in Ljubljana

note: The foundation of Emona is dated c. 14–15 CE; the early medieval period is summarised in one entry.
